subject: Translate R basic plot to ggplot2

messages.author: c285c335a5fbc044
messages.subject: Translate R basic plot to ggplot2
parts:
Dear ggplot users,

I have created the following graph using basic R commands

A <- subset(Summary, A1 == 0 & A2 == 0)
B <- subset(Summary, A1 >= 1)


A.tmp <- hist(A[,'A1'], breaks = (1,2,3,4,5,10), plot = FALSE)
B.tmp <- hist(B[,A1'], breaks = (1,2,3,4,5,10), plot = FALSE)

plot.new()

plot(A.tmp$counts/sum(A.tmp$counts), type = 'b',
axes = FALSE, ylim = c(0, 0.45), pch = 20, xlim = c(0.5, 4.5), cex =
0.8,
lty = 1, col = 'black)

lines(B.tmp$counts/sum(B.tmp$counts), type = 'b',
axes = FALSE, ylim = c(0, 0.45), pch = 20, xlim = c(0.5, 4.5), cex =
0.8, lty = 2, col = 'red')

axis(1, at = seq(0.5, 5, by = 1), labels = FALSE)
axis(1, at = seq(1, 4, by = 1), labels =
c("1-2","2-3","3-4","4-5","5-10") tick = FALSE)
axis(2)

legend(x = 3, y = 0.1, c("A" , "B"), cex = 0.8, col = c("black",
"red"), lty = c(1,2));

abline(v = 2.5, col = "black")

I made some changes to names so it's clearer. The values in A1 are
integers from 1-300. I tried to do the same with ggplot but keep
getting errors like ggplot does not know how to deal with this data
etc. Is there a way to plot something exactly like in the example
using ggplot? Thanks for help


Maria

answer. Preferably the result of dput(Summary), though possibly only a
subset of that if Summary is large (over 100 rows, say).
